text.p: Berkshire Hathaway Inc and FlightSafety International Inc said on Tuesday that they have executed a definitive merger agreement in which FlightSafety will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire.

In the merger, valued at approximately $1.5 billion, FlightSafety shareholders can elect to receive for each of their shares of FlightSafety either $50 in cash or $48 in Class A or Class B common stock of Berkshire.
The deal is subject to a limitation that the amount of cash to be issued in the merger will not exceed 58 percent of the total value of consideration to be received in the merger.

Consummation of the merger is subject to the approval of two thirds of the outstanding shares of FlightSafety. The firms said that shareholders representing in excess of 37 percent of FlightSafety's common stock have stated that they intend to vote in favor of the transaction.

The number of shares of Berkshire to be received under the stock election would be determined based on the market price for Berkshire shares during a five-day trading period ending the day prior to the FlightSafety shareholders' meeting to approve the merger.

The companies said board of directors of FlightSafety has unanimously approved the merger agreement and recommends it to the shareholders for approval. The merger is expected to close near the end of 1996 or early 1997.
The companies anticipated that the merger will qualify under the Internal Revenue Code as a tax-free reorganization for those FlightSafety shareholders electing to receive Berkshire common stock.

Albert L. Ueltschi, chairman and chief executive officer of FlightSafety, said in a statement that he expects to continue running Flightsafety, which provides high-technology training to operators of aircraft and ships globally.
